In a fully off-shell calculation, we provide results for the leading electroweak contribution of $\mathcal{O}\left(α^6\right)$ and the corresponding corrections of $\mathcal{O}\left(α^7\right)$ and $\mathcal{O}\left(α_\text{s} α^6\right)$ for fiducial cross sections and a selection of differential distributions.

AI.tldr: The paper presents calculations of NLO QCD and electroweak corrections for vector-boson scattering processes at the LHC, specifically $	ext{p}	ext{p} 	o 	ext{ℓ}^+ ν_	ext{ℓ} + 4	ext{j}$.
AI.motivation: Improving the precision of theoretical predictions for vector-boson scattering, given recent measurements at the LHC and future experimental plans.
AI.method: Calculations involve NLO QCD and electroweak corrections in a fully off-shell framework for the process and focus on fiducial regions.
AI.result: Leading electroweak contributions of $	ext{O}(α^6)$ and related corrections of $	ext{O}(α^7)$ and $	ext{O}(α_	ext{s} α^6)$ were provided for both fiducial cross sections and differential distributions.
AI.conclusion: The results offer important theoretical insights needed for future experiments aiming for precise measurements in vector-boson scattering.

title: String dynamics of a (2+1)D U(1) quantum link model on a digital quantum computer
summary: The (2+1)D U(1) pure gauge theory always exists in the confining phase, with strings of non-zero string tension giving a characteristic linear potential between static charges. This makes it a useful testing ground for quantum computing methods designed to study string dynamics of confining gauge theories. Here we implement a minimal U(1) quantum link model on a quantum computer with qubit degrees of freedom representing the dual height variables of the model. This facilitates an efficient realization of plaquette interactions and enables effective calculations of real-time dynamics that are inaccessible to traditional quantum Monte Carlo. A specifically tailored lattice geometry is chosen to match the heavy-hexagonal geometry of the IBM quantum hardware used here, minimizing non-adjacent qubit interactions. By performing quantum quenches from a simple initial string state, we probe the transverse quantum fluctuations of the string before it thermalizes. Our experimental results from digital quantum simulations, with up to 112 qubits, show good agreement with reference tensor-network calculations at short times and with thermal averages at long times. Near the phase transition, the quench dynamics exhibit large fluctuations of the initial string that extend across both spatial dimensions of the lattice. Nonetheless, our error-mitigated estimators from the quantum hardware also give accurate predictions in that regime, with noise-induced violations of local gauge symmetries comparable to finite-bond-dimension tensor-network results.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a quantum link model for studying string dynamics in (2+1)D U(1) gauge theory on quantum hardware, achieving effective real-time simulations and accurate results compared to tensor-network calculations.
AI.motivation: To explore the dynamics of confining gauge theories using quantum computing methods, particularly in the context of U(1) pure gauge theory.
AI.method: A minimal U(1) quantum link model is implemented on quantum hardware, utilizing qubits to represent dual height variables, with tailored lattice geometry matching the hardware design to enable efficient calculations of plaquette interactions.
AI.result: Digital quantum simulations up to 112 qubits demonstrate agreement with tensor-network calculations at short times and with thermal averages at long times, revealing significant fluctuations near phase transitions.
AI.conclusion: The study validates the use of quantum hardware for probing string dynamics in gauge theories, with accurate predictions even in regimes affected by noise.

title: Theory Calculations for LDMX and LOHENGRIN beyond Coherent Bethe-Heitler Scattering
summary: The Light Dark Matter eXperiment (LDMX), DarkSHINE, and LOHENGRIN are proposed new experiments. They aim to search for missing momentum signals sourced by the direct production of dark photons with masses in the MeV-GeV range in bremsstrahlung processes, in which an electron beam of a few GeV scatters off a fixed target. So far, the signal characteristics, i.e. the behavior of the recoiling electron, have mostly been studied in coherent Bethe-Heitler electron-nucleus scattering with a dark photon that couples only to the Standard Model charged leptons. In this work, we present the calculations of the differential cross sections of all contributing real emission processes up to third order in the electromagnetic fine structure constant and fourth order in the kinetic mixing parameter associated with the dark photon. We consider a dark photon coupling to both the beam electron and the hadronic target and we take into account the scattering off both the target nucleus and its nuclear constituents. Besides real emission processes, we also discuss virtual dark photon contributions and their relevance for the signal prediction. After discussing the different phase space regions and constraints emerging from the experimental setups, we show numerical results of the cross sections and differential distributions, including the signal and dominant background. Within our framework, we find that the LOHENGRIN experiment will require an extension of its HCAL to effectively veto background processes originating from diffractive scattering. Apart from that, the contributions beyond coherent Bethe-Heitler scattering, in the presence of realistic experimental selections, have only a limited effect on the predicted signal and background in the relevant dark photon mass range.

AI.tldr: The paper discusses calculations for new experiments LDMX, DarkSHINE, and LOHENGRIN that aim to detect dark photons through bremsstrahlung processes and presents differential cross sections calculations critical for understanding signals and backgrounds related to dark photon detection.
AI.motivation: To search for dark photons in the MeV-GeV mass range using new experimental setups and to understand the scattering processes involved.
AI.method: Calculating differential cross sections for all contributing real emission processes up to third order in the fine structure constant and fourth order in kinetic mixing; considering both target nucleus and constituents.
AI.result: Numerical results are presented, which suggest that while contributions beyond coherent Bethe-Heitler scattering have limited effects, the LOHENGRIN experiment will need an HCAL extension for better background control.
AI.conclusion: The findings indicate limitations in the impact of complex processes on signal predictions, emphasizing the need for specific experimental adaptations.

title: Two Flavon Froggatt-Nielsen Models with Genetic Algorithms
summary: We present the first systematic and comprehensive scan of two-flavon Froggatt-Nielsen (FN) models, employing artificial intelligence techniques to explore the high-dimensional, mixed discrete-continuous parameter space. Extending the standard single-flavon FN framework to a two-flavon setup in which separate flavon fields couple independently to the up- and down-type sectors, we demonstrate that the relative phase between their vacuum expectation values (vevs) provides a natural and generic source of CP violation absent in single-flavon models. To explore this enlarged model space, we cast the search for phenomenologically viable models as a multi-objective optimisation problem, formulating each experimental constraint as a separate objective, and employ the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III to simultaneously fit all 18 FN charges, 45 Wilson coefficients, and flavon parameters to both the quark and lepton sectors. Our approach requires no separate training phase and identifies phenomenologically viable models orders of magnitude faster than prior reinforcement learning methods. Imposing experimental constraints on CKM and PMNS mixing angles and CP phases, charged fermion masses, and neutrino squared-mass differences, we discover over $100\,000$ unique viable models with a remarkably low duplication rate, indicating that the space of valid two-flavon FN realisations has not been exhausted. Both Normal and Inverted neutrino mass squared orderings are realised, with the relative hierarchy between the flavon vevs producing qualitatively distinct predictions for the effective neutrinoless double beta decay mass $m_{ee}$. We further demonstrate the existence of minimal FN realisations with maximal flavon exponent as small as three, and of models reproducing charged fermion masses to within $6\%$ without any dedicated continuous parameter optimisation.

AI.tldr: The paper systematically scans two-flavon Froggatt-Nielsen models using AI, revealing comprehensive results and over 100,000 unique models that exhibit enhanced CP violation and fit various experimental constraints efficiently.
AI.motivation: To explore the two-flavon Froggatt-Nielsen model's potential in generating CP violation and to find phenomenologically viable models efficiently.
AI.method: Artificial intelligence techniques are employed, formulating the search as a multi-objective optimization problem using the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III to fit a large parameter space.
AI.result: The analysis yields over 100,000 unique viable models with low duplication, demonstrating a vast space of valid two-flavon FN realizations.
AI.conclusion: The study not only identifies minimal FN realizations with low flavon exponent but also presents models reproducing fermion masses to within 6%, indicating significant findings in neutrino mass hierarchies and effective decay mass predictions.

title: Subsystem Quantum Error Correction for Noisy Quantum Metrology
summary: Quantum error correction has been successfully applied to enhance the precision of parameter estimation in the presence of noise. Nonetheless, existing methods require a number of noiseless, controllable ancillae and lack efficient encoding and decoding procedures. In this Letter, we demonstrate that subsystem error correction provides a new direction that can substantially simplify the metrological protocol. We derive general conditions under which subsystem stabilizer codes achieve the Heisenberg limit and show that, for broad classes of noise, this can be realized by syndrome-free protocols using at most a single ancilla qubit. Furthermore, we extend this framework to dynamical error correction and show that Floquet codes can protect time-dependent metrological signals in reaching the Heisenberg limit.

AI.tldr: Subsystem error correction simplifies quantum parameter estimation, achieving Heisenberg limit with fewer ancillae.
AI.motivation: Existing quantum error correction methods for parameter estimation are resource-intensive and inefficient.
AI.method: By employing subsystem stabilizer codes, we derive conditions for achieving the Heisenberg limit, minimizing the need for multiple ancillae, utilizing syndrome-free protocols.
AI.result: Demonstrated achievement of Heisenberg limit with minimal ancilla qubits and extended the approach to dynamical error correction using Floquet codes.
AI.conclusion: Subsystem error correction represents a significant advance, making quantum metrology more efficient and feasible.

title: The $B^+ \to K^+ ν\bar ν$ decay as a QCD axion search: comparing reinterpretation approaches
summary: Two recent independent analyses of Belle II $B^+ \! \to \! K^+ν\barν$ data yield limits on ${\mathcal B}(B^+ \! \to \! K^+ a)$ -- the two-body mode to a light invisible particle such as the QCD axion -- differing by a factor of roughly four; we trace this to the choice of kinematic variable space. The central figure of merit is the resolution in the reconstructed di-neutrino invariant mass $q^2_{\rm rec}$: fine-grained binning resolves the narrow axion signal, while coarse binning dilutes it into a background-dominated range. A BDT axis trained on $B^+ \! \to \! K^+ν\barν$ adds little discriminating power for $B^+ \! \to \! K^+ a$, as this axis is largely uncorrelated with $q^2$. These expectations are confirmed by a set of numerical tests. The subleading shape systematics omitted from our $q^2_{\rm rec}$-based approach {\em lower}, not raise, the $B^+ \! \to \! K^+ a$ limit: by better accommodating the $B^+ \! \to \! K^+ν\barν$ shape, they leave less room for the axion signal, making our $q^2_{\rm rec}$-based bound conservative, if anything. A dedicated reanalysis confirms that the kinematic-axes choice alone accounts for the factor-of-four sensitivity difference, and that the $B^+ \! \to \! K^+ a$ bound varies sizeably within the $q^2_{\rm rec}\timesη({\rm BDT}_2)$ space, depending on the SM-likeness of $B^+ \! \to \! K^+ν\barν$, thus losing the dual-probe feature of our $q^2_{\rm rec}$-based approach. These results point to a broader consideration: likelihoods dominated by BDT variables are of limited use for reinterpretations when the signal shape differs appreciably from the BDT's training signal. We therefore advocate that experimental collaborations publish likelihood projections in physical variable spaces alongside BDT-based likelihoods, to maximise the reinterpretability of their measurements.

AI.tldr: Two analyses of Belle II data show differing limits on the decay mode $B^+ \to K^+ a$, attributed to the chosen kinematic variables. Fine binning improves signal resolution, while BDT offers minimal benefit. A reanalysis suggests BDT likelihoods may hinder reinterpretation due to signal shape discrepancies, advocating for physical variable publication alongside BDT results.
AI.motivation: To resolve discrepancies in limits on the $B^+ \to K^+ a$ decay mode derived from Belle II data analyses.
AI.method: Comparative analysis of two approaches: one with fine-grained binning of the di-neutrino invariant mass $q^2_{m rec}$ and another utilizing a BDT axis. Numerical tests are performed to assess sensitivity differences based on kinematic variables.
AI.result: The choice of kinematic variables alone accounts for a factor of four difference in sensitivity. The analysis revealed that BDT likelihoods do not enhance discrimination power for the axion signal and may obscure interpretations.
AI.conclusion: The authors recommend that experimental collaborations provide likelihood projections in both physical variable spaces and BDT-based likelihoods to improve reinterpretability of measurements.

title: Quantum Dynamics from Lax Pair Theory: A Reconstruction from Spectrum Preservation
summary: We reconstruct unitary quantum dynamics from a minimal axiomatic foundation built on Hilbert-space observables and isospectral evolution. The only dynamical assumption is that physical time evolution is a continuous one-parameter flow of Hermitian observables that preserves their spectra, i.e. the possible outcomes of measurement. We show that this assumption is already sufficient to force the Lax form of quantum dynamics. The Heisenberg equation, the time-dependent and time-independent Schrödinger equations, conservation laws, and good quantum numbers then follow as theorems rather than postulates. In this formulation, Lax pair theory supplies the missing dynamical bridge between the measurement structure of a Hilbert space and standard quantum evolution: the Hamiltonian is not assumed, but emerges as the generator required for an isospectral observable flow.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes a framework for unitary quantum dynamics using minimal axioms from Hilbert-space observables and isospectral evolution, leading to key quantum equations as theorems.
AI.motivation: To provide a foundational perspective on unitary quantum dynamics that connects measurement and dynamical evolution through axioms rather than conventional postulates.
AI.method: The approach leverages isospectral evolution and continuous flows of Hermitian observables to derive quantum equations and conservation laws.
AI.result: The derivation includes the Heisenberg equation, Schrödinger equations, and conservation laws as theorems, demonstrating consistency between measurement outcomes and quantum dynamics.
AI.conclusion: Lax pair theory reveals the Hamiltonian as an emergent generator in quantum dynamics, unifying the concepts of measurement and evolution in a rigorous framework.

title: The Simplest Dirac Scoto-Seesaw Realization
summary: We present a simple Dirac scoto-seesaw framework based on the anomaly-free $U(1)_{B-L}$ charge assignment $(-4,-4,5)$ for $ν_R$. This chiral charge assignment naturally accounts for the observed neutrino mass-squared differences, with $Δm^2_{\rm atm}$ generated at tree level and $Δm^2_{\rm sol}$ arising radiatively. After the spontaneous breaking of gauged $U(1)_{B-L}$, a residual $Z_6$ symmetry stabilizes the dark matter candidate. We investigate two minimal realizations of the framework, finding that both normal and inverted orderings are viable in one case, whereas only normal ordering survives in the other, with distinctive features for neutrino observables. Moreover, the chiral nature of the $U(1)_{B-L}$ charges suppresses the dilepton branching fraction of $Z'$, resulting in weaker ATLAS mass bounds than in the conventional vector $B-L$ scenario, thereby easing constraints on the dark sector. We explore the dark matter phenomenology of the singlet scalar and fermionic dark matter candidates. While singlet scalar DM is often severely constrained, the presence of the $Z'$ portal together with annihilation and co-annihilation channels substantially broadens the allowed parameter space. Thus, the framework offers a predictive scenario for neutrino and dark matter phenomenology that can be probed in future experiments.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a Dirac scoto-seesaw framework that utilizes a chiral anomaly-free $U(1)_{B-L}$ charge assignment to explain neutrino mass differences and dark matter stability, presenting two realizations with different neutrino patterns and exploring their implications for dark matter.
AI.motivation: To provide a unified framework addressing neutrino mass generation and dark matter stability under a chiral $U(1)_{B-L}$ charge assignment.
AI.method: The paper employs a Dirac scoto-seesaw mechanism with specific anomaly-free charge assignments, analyzing two minimal realizations to explore neutrino mass ordering and dark matter phenomenology.
AI.result: Both normal and inverted neutrino orderings are viable in one scenario, while the other supports only normal ordering; the framework produces lighter mass bounds for dark matter candidates due to suppressed dilepton branching fractions.
AI.conclusion: The developed framework demonstrates predictive qualities for neutrino and dark matter interactions, offering avenues for experimental exploration.

title: Topological Quantum Interferometry
summary: Structured light provides high-dimensional Hilbert spaces holding tremendous potential for fundamental quantum optics and quantum technologies. However, existing characterization methods, like Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interference, typically assume perfectly tuned conditions, overlooking the geometric physics governing spatial mode evolution. Here, we establish topological quantum interferometry driven by an interaction-based geometric phase, the exchange Berry phase (BPX). Our formalism generalizes $q$-plate state generation and characterization to arbitrary topological charges and (de)tuning conditions, demonstrating that BPX acts as a geometric marker governing spatial interference. We show BPX serves as a deterministic control parameter, decomposing two-photon spatial patterns into geometry-dictated fundamental modes. This mapping reveals topological invariants and phase singularities that function as a non-tomographic witness for state dimensionality estimation, circumventing full-state reconstruction. Being device-independent and highly scalable, this approach enables scalable high-dimensional characterization and topologically protected state selection, with direct applicability to quantum metrology and high-capacity quantum networks.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a method for characterizing high-dimensional quantum states using topological quantum interferometry and the Berry phase, allowing for scalable applications in quantum technologies.
AI.motivation: To address the limitations of current methods in characterizing structured light and to enhance the understanding of spatial mode evolution in quantum optics.
AI.method: The authors develop a topological quantum interferometry formalism driven by the exchange Berry phase (BPX), generalizing state generation and characterization to any topological charge under various tuning conditions.
AI.result: BPX serves as a geometric marker that decomposes two-photon spatial patterns into fundamental modes determined by geometry, revealing invariants and phase singularities useful for non-tomographic state dimensionality estimation.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method is device-independent and scalable, offering significant advantages for quantum metrology and the development of high-capacity quantum networks.

title: Addressing uncertainties of model predictions for extensive air showers initiated by high energy cosmic rays
summary: A new Monte Carlo generator of hadronic collisions, QGSb, is applied for studying model uncertainties regarding calculations of the development of extensive air showers (EAS) initiated by interactions of high energy cosmic rays in the atmosphere. More specifically, we investigate possibilities to modify the model predictions for two EAS characteristics mostly used in experimental studies of cosmic ray composition: air shower maximum depth and the muon number at ground level. For all the considered modifications of the model, we discuss in some detail the underlying physics mechanisms and investigate the impact of the changes, regarding a comparison of the model results to relevant accelerator data.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a new Monte Carlo generator, QGSb, for analyzing uncertainties in extensive air shower (EAS) characteristics related to cosmic ray interactions.
AI.motivation: To address model uncertainties in EAS simulations, specifically related to high-energy cosmic ray interactions in the atmosphere.
AI.method: The study uses QGSb to modify predictions for air shower maximum depth and muon number, analyzing the underlying physics mechanisms.
AI.result: The paper systematically evaluates changes in model predictions and compares them with relevant accelerator data.
AI.conclusion: Findings suggest significant impacts of model modifications on EAS characteristics, which can enhance understanding of cosmic ray composition.

title: Sparse positive maps on qutrits with exact nondecomposability thresholds and PPT-entanglement transitions
summary: We study a family of sparse positive maps on qutrits for which positivity, decomposability, and PPT entanglement can all be analysed explicitly. The block structure of the associated Choi matrices reduces positivity to a Hermitian biquadratic form and leads to exact positivity boundaries for three representative parametric families. For the same families we determine the exact transition between decomposable and non-decomposable maps and construct associated PPT states of two classes. The first consists of witness-adapted deformations naturally tied to the non-decomposability analysis. The second consists of analytically tractable families whose full PPT-entangled branch is detected by fixed positive maps, yielding exact thresholds between separability and bound entanglement. For the trace-preserving subclass, we further compare positivity with a recent eigenvalue bound for 2-positive maps, thereby making the gap between positivity and higher-order positivity fully explicit within this family.

AI.tldr: This study investigates sparse positive maps on qutrits, analyzing their positivity, decomposability, and PPT entanglement through Choi matrices, yielding explicit thresholds for separability and bound entanglement.
AI.motivation: To gain deeper insights into the behavior of sparse positive maps on qutrits and to establish clear criteria for their entanglement properties.
AI.method: The study employs an analysis of the Choi matrices of the maps to transform the problem into a Hermitian biquadratic form, allowing for calculating positivity boundaries and transition thresholds between decomposable and non-decomposable maps.
AI.result: Identified exact positivity boundaries for three parametric families of maps and constructed associated PPT states, revealing conditions for separability, non-decomposability, and bound entanglement.
AI.conclusion: The analysis provides a comprehensive understanding of the relationships between positivity, decomposability, and entanglement properties in qutrits, as well as clarifying the distinction between positivity and higher-order positivity in trace-preserving maps.

title: Three-particle di-light-cone distribution amplitudes of the $B$-meson in heavy-quark effective theory
summary: We present a systematic study of the three-particle di-light-cone distribution amplitudes (DLCDAs) of the $B$-meson. They are defined through $B$-meson--to--vacuum matrix elements of trilocal HQET operators, in which the light antiquark and the gluon field-strength tensor are located on two back-to-back light rays. In this sense, the DLCDAs generalise the conventional $B$-meson light-cone distribution amplitudes to configurations where soft fields couple to collinear degrees of freedom in two distinct directions. As such, they parametrise the non-perturbative dynamics associated with non-factorisable soft-gluon contributions in rare and non-leptonic exclusive $B$-meson decays. We derive the complete Lorentz decomposition of the matrix elements of generic trilocal operators, identify eight independent DLCDAs, and organise them in a basis of definite twist. Using local operator identities and equations-of-motion constraints, we obtain tree-level relations for their normalisation integrals and first moments in terms of a minimal set of hadronic parameters. These relations allow us to construct simple momentum-space models for all independent DLCDAs. For the leading-twist distribution, we further incorporate the perturbative radiative tail at order $α_s$ and discuss its impact on the resulting parametrisation.

AI.tldr: This study explores the three-particle di-light-cone distribution amplitudes (DLCDAs) of $B$-mesons, focusing on their structure and implications for non-perturbative dynamics in $B$-decays.
AI.motivation: To better understand the non-factorisable contributions of soft gluons in rare and non-leptonic exclusive $B$-meson decays and how they affect theoretical predictions.
AI.method: The study involves deriving the complete Lorentz decomposition of trilocal HQET operator matrix elements, identifying eight independent DLCDAs, and using local operator identities to relate them to hadronic parameters.
AI.result: The authors establish relations between the independent DLCDAs and hadronic parameters, and present momentum-space models while considering the perturbative radiative tail for the leading-twist distribution.
AI.conclusion: The findings enhance our understanding of the non-perturbative dynamics in $B$-decays and provide a framework for modeling DLCDAs relevant to rare processes.

title: Robust Generation of Topological Biphoton Mode via Adiabatic Passage
summary: Topological waveguide arrays support robust mode propagation in the presence of fabrication imperfections, providing a significant advantage for on-chip quantum information processing. However, this robustness does not fully extend to nonlinear biphoton generation. Structural disorder can enhance the excitation of non-topological biphoton modes during nonlinear interactions, which degrades the quantum properties of the generated state. To overcome this limitation, we propose an adiabatic passage that connects an isolated site to a topological defect array. By initiating the nonlinear process in a strongly isolated regime, nonlinear coupling to unwanted modes is effectively suppressed, thereby preserving the Schmidt number of the generated state. The subsequent adiabatic connection facilitates the high fidelity transfer of the generated biphoton into the topological biphoton mode. Our numerical simulations demonstrate that, unlike conventional topological structures, the adiabatic scheme maintains both high biphoton fidelity and a unit Schmidt number in the presence of waveguide gap disorder. Furthermore, we show that this robustness extends to path entangled NOON states, achieving a near-unity quantum interference visibility. Our approach provides a practical design strategy for disorder-tolerant integrated quantum photonic devices.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes an adiabatic passage to improve biphoton generation in topological waveguide arrays, overcoming challenges posed by structural disorder.
AI.motivation: To address the degradation of quantum properties in biphoton generation due to structural disorder in topological waveguide arrays.
AI.method: An adiabatic passage connects an isolated site to a topological defect array, initiating the nonlinear process in an isolated regime to suppress unwanted mode coupling.
AI.result: Numerical simulations show that the adiabatic scheme maintains high biphoton fidelity and a unit Schmidt number despite waveguide disorder, and extends to path entangled NOON states with high quantum interference visibility.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method offers a practical design for disorder-tolerant integrated quantum photonic devices.

title: Dyonic lattices, $θ$-angles and axions in the Standard Model
summary: We investigate the implications of the Witten effect in the Standard Model with a general global gauge group structure and determine the values of the three $θ$-parameters that lead to distinct families of allowed spectra of dyons. We construct and classify the corresponding dyonic charge lattices consistent with the Standard Model gauge structure. This approach enables us to re-derive the known global-group--dependent periodicities of the $θ$ angles and to determine all CP-invariant points in $θ$-space. The electromagnetic subgroup $U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$ is shown to arise \emph{prior} to electroweak symmetry breaking by factoring out the effect of the anomalous $B+L$ transformations, which reduces the physical $θ$-parameter space from a three-torus to a two-torus. Our phenomenological conclusions include an observation that a discovery of a $U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$ monopole carrying non-zero electric charge would determine the last remaining unknown parameter of the Standard Model. Lastly we study how $θ$-space shapes axion physics with emphasis on the axion-photon coupling and show that a single axion is insufficient to render the Standard Model vacuum fully CP invariant.

AI.tldr: This paper explores the Witten effect in the Standard Model, investigating the implications of $θ$-parameters on dyonic spectra and CP invariance, with connections to axion physics.
AI.motivation: To understand the implications of the Witten effect within a general framework of the Standard Model and its gauge group structure.
AI.method: The authors classify dyonic charge lattices and analyze $θ$-parameters and their periodicities, as well as the effects of anomalous transformations on the structure of $θ$-space.
AI.result: The research reveals the connection between $U(1)_{	ext{em}}$ and the Standard Model parameters, indicating that a $U(1)_{	ext{em}}$ monopole discovery could complete the parameter space of the Standard Model.
AI.conclusion: The findings emphasize that a single axion does not achieve full CP invariance in the Standard Model and that the behavior of $θ$-space is crucial for axion physics.

title: QMCtwin: Master-Equation Simulation of Syndrome Statistics Beyond Pauli Noise
summary: As quantum error correction moves toward large-scale experimental implementations, decoder performance increasingly depends on how faithfully hardware noise is translated into syndrome statistics. Standard stabilizer workflows achieve scalability by replacing device dynamics with stochastic Pauli or detector-error models, but this compression can discard coherent phase information, nonunital drift, continuous-time effects of always-on couplings, and correlations generated by simultaneous Hamiltonian and dissipative evolution. Here we present QMCtwin, a sign-problem-suppressed quantum Monte Carlo framework for master-equation simulation of QEC circuits, and apply it to a full syndrome-extraction round of a distance-$7$ rotated surface code with $97$ physical qubits. The open-system model includes realistic superconducting-device noise mechanisms such as relaxation, pure dephasing, coherent gate miscalibration, residual $ZZ$ crosstalk, and drive-qubit detuning. By directly estimating syndrome observables from the QMC-generated stochastic density matrix estimator, we compare the master-equation dynamics with their Pauli-twirled Clifford simulation counterparts. QMCtwin predicts syndrome-extraction biases and correlations between syndromes and proxies of logical-string-parity that are absent or strongly suppressed in the stochastic Pauli description. We introduce information-theoretic diagnostics that further quantify how information concerning syndromes versus string-parity proxies differs between the realistic master-equation simulation and the corresponding Pauli-twirled model. These results show that QMC-based master-equation digital twins can expose noise features hidden by conventional Pauli/Clifford noise models and provide a practical path toward more accurate decoder-facing syndrome models.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces QMCtwin, a quantum Monte Carlo framework designed to simulate quantum error correction circuits more accurately by incorporating realistic noise factors and preserving coherent information that standard models might neglect.
AI.motivation: The need for improved decoder performance in quantum error correction (QEC) as experimental implementations scale and the limitations of conventional noise modeling approaches.
AI.method: QMCtwin employs a quantum Monte Carlo framework to simulate master-equation dynamics for a distance-7 rotated surface code involving 97 physical qubits, considering various realistic noise mechanisms.
AI.result: QMCtwin predicts distinct syndrome-extraction biases and correlations absent in conventional Pauli model simulations, demonstrating the importance of realistic noise features.
AI.conclusion: The study illustrates that QMC-based simulations can reveal critical noise characteristics overlooked in conventional models, enhancing the accuracy of decoder-facing syndrome models for quantum error correction."

title: Random Local Stabilizer Codes in Three Dimensions without String or Self-Similar Fractal Logical Operators
comment: 20 pages, 11 figures. Repository for data: https://github.com/hanyanphysics/QTRCC
summary: Quantum error-correcting codes (QECs) are essential components quantum computation and have deep connections to quantum phases of matter. A key obstruction to passive self-correcting QECs is the presence of string logical operators, which can generate logical errors through constant-energy-barrier processes. Haah's Codes (fracton codes) showed that three-dimensional stabilizer codes can forbid such string logical operators, but their translation-invariant structure supports self-similar fractal logical operators with a logarithmic energy barrier. We introduce the qutrit random cubic codes, a family of local qutrit Calderbank-Shor-Steane stabilizer Hamiltonians with similar cube-check structure as Haah's Code 1 but built from spatially varying stabilizers. We prove that these models retain the no-string property and numerically observe that they have properties distinct from translation-invariant fracton codes: the smallest ground-state degeneracy exponent is $k=2$ for odd $L$ and $k=4$ for even $L$; noncontractible plane-logical operators span the entire logical space; and charge-push diagnostics show that the self-similar fractal operators are absent. These results demonstrate that constrained randomness can fundamentally change the nature of stabilizer codes and improve their self-correction properties. They further point to broader families of quantum error-correcting codes and quantum phases beyond canonical topological and fracton orders.

AI.tldr: Introduces qutrit random cubic codes to overcome limitations of string logical operators in quantum error-correcting codes, demonstrating improved self-correction properties and unique characteristics compared to traditional fracton codes.
AI.motivation: To address the challenges posed by string logical operators in passive self-correcting quantum error-correcting codes (QECs).
AI.method: Developed qutrit random cubic codes with varying stabilizers that maintain the no-string property while utilizing a cube-check structure similar to Haah's Codes.
AI.result: Showed distinct properties from translation-invariant fracton codes, including ground-state degeneracies of $k=2$ for odd $L$ and $k=4$ for even $L$, and absence of self-similar fractal operators.
AI.conclusion: Constrained randomness in stabilizer codes leads to improved self-correction and reveals new families of QECs and quantum phases beyond traditional classifications.

title: Renormalization of axial anomaly in SU(N)$\times$U(1)
summary: Defining $γ_5$ within dimensional regularization remains a fundamental challenge. Larin's prescription addresses this by introducing additional renormalization constants to restore standard and chiral Ward identities. While these constants are known up to four loops in pure quantum chromodynamics, current precision Standard Model phenomenology requires extending these corrections to mixed gauge sectors. In this article, we propose a novel technique utilizing form factors and the universality of infrared divergences to compute these constants. Applying this framework, we present the new three-loop results for the renormalization constants, as well as the pure-singlet contributions to the quark axial-vector form factor, for a mixed $SU(N) \times U(1)$ gauge group.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the calculation of renormalization constants for $\gamma_5$ in dimensional regularization, extending previous methods to mixed gauge sectors and presenting new results at three loops.
AI.motivation: The need for accurate renormalization constants to uphold standard and chiral Ward identities in high-precision Standard Model predictions.
AI.method: A novel technique leveraging form factors and the universality of infrared divergences to compute the necessary renormalization constants.
AI.result: New three-loop results for renormalization constants and pure-singlet contributions to the quark axial-vector form factor in a mixed $SU(N) \times U(1)$ gauge context.
AI.conclusion: The proposed technique successfully extends the calculations to mixed gauge sectors, providing essential insights for precision calculations in the Standard Model.

title: Purity and bound energy in ancilla-assisted work extraction
summary: We investigate ancilla-assisted work extraction in quantum batteries from the perspective of bound energy and purity. We show that the bound energy of the reduced system provides a tight upper bound to the daemonic gain and that this bound is saturated for globally pure system--ancilla states. Motivated by this relation, we introduce a purity-based gain that qualitatively predicts the daemonic gain without requiring explicit optimization over measurements. We further introduce a protocol to analyze the role of dissipation and intrinsic interactions on daemonic gain. Under a collective environment, dissipation can dynamically generate and stabilize finite daemonic gain through environment-induced correlations. In interacting systems, level crossings and spectral restructuring strongly modify the attainable gain through their influence on the accessible bound energy. Our results demonstrate that daemonic gain is governed not only by correlations, but also by the spectral structure of the underlying Hamiltonian and information loss captured by bound energy and purity.

AI.tldr: This paper explores ancilla-assisted work extraction in quantum batteries, focusing on the relationship between bound energy and purity to predict daemonic gain.
AI.motivation: To understand how bound energy and purity influence work extraction efficiency in quantum batteries.
AI.method: Introduces a purity-based gain metric and a protocol for analyzing dissipation and interactions on daemonic gain under different environmental conditions.
AI.result: Demonstrates a clear connection between bound energy, purity, and the daemonic gain, revealing how dissipation and spectral structure impact energy extraction.
AI.conclusion: Daemonic gain is influenced by correlations, the Hamiltonian's spectral structure, and information loss, indicating a complex interplay between these factors.

title: Revisiting the role of saturation in diffractive vector meson production
summary: We perform a global Bayesian analysis of coherent and incoherent diffractive $\mathrm{J}/ψ$ photoproduction in $γ+p$ and $γ+\mathrm{Pb}$ collisions using a Color Glass Condensate (CGC)-based framework and ultraperipheral collision data from the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), corrected for the expected effect of electromagnetic dissociation (EMD). Using Gaussian-process emulators of the underlying CGC calculations, we infer model parameters from a combined set of HERA and LHC measurements. We find that the $γ+\mathrm{Pb}$ data with EMD correction substantially reduce the previously observed tension between proton and nuclear datasets, enabling a consistent simultaneous description of diffractive $\mathrm{J}/ψ$ production in $γ+p$ and $γ+\mathrm{Pb}$ collisions within the CGC framework.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a global Bayesian analysis of diffractive $	ext{J}/ψ$ photoproduction in proton and lead collisions using a CGC framework, revealing improved model consistency through EMD correction of LHC data.
AI.motivation: To address discrepancies in diffractive $	ext{J}/ψ$ photoproduction data from proton and nuclear collisions by employing a coherent theoretical framework.
AI.method: Utilizing a Color Glass Condensate model and Gaussian-process emulators to analyze ultraperipheral collision data, along with a Bayesian statistical approach to infer model parameters.
AI.result: The application of EMD corrections to the $γ+	ext{Pb}$ dataset alleviates tensions between datasets from different collision types, enhancing model consistency.
AI.conclusion: Simultaneous modeling of diffractive $	ext{J}/ψ$ production across different collision types is achieved, supporting the validity of the CGC framework in addressing previously observed discrepancies.

title: QMaxCal: Path-Space Regularization for Open Quantum Control via Girsanov's Theorem
summary: Reliable quantum control in the presence of decoherence requires policies that combat the effect of environmental noise on the controlled dynamics. Open quantum systems under continuous monitoring generate classical measurement records whose drift depends on the noise experienced by the system; the records of two evolutions sharing the same decoherence channels differ only in this drift, so Girsanov's theorem yields a closed-form, differentiable estimator of the KL divergence between their trajectory distributions. We instantiate this estimator with two physically motivated reference measures, yielding two regularizers that both drive the system toward states where the effects of decoherence are minimal: the Wiener KL (KL_W), which is empirically more effective under certain conditions on the noise model, and the drift-variance regularizer (R_DV), which works for all noise models. Both are qualitatively distinct from existing penalties on control fluence or smoothness: they penalize the observable consequences of control on the decoherence channels rather than the control amplitude itself. The regularizers outperform unregularized gradient-based and reinforcement-learning baselines across a range of open quantum systems -- including single- and multi-qubit benchmarks and a multi-qubit chain calibrated to a published snapshot of the IBM Kingston processor -- along several axes of evaluation: final-state fidelity, robustness to mismatch in the assumed noise model (gains grow from +17 pp at training noise to +27 pp under 2.5x noise mismatch), and occupation of forbidden states. The regularizers reduce infidelity by up to 50%, with ~16% gains on the calibrated IBM Kingston chain.

AI.tldr: The paper presents regularizers to enhance quantum control under decoherence, showing improved performance in various open quantum systems.
AI.motivation: To develop effective strategies for quantum control against decoherence, addressing the challenges posed by environmental noise.
AI.method: Utilizing Girsanov's theorem to derive differentiable estimators of KL divergence, two regularizers (Wiener KL and Drift-Variance) are introduced, which focus on minimizing decoherence effects instead of control amplitude.
AI.result: The introduced regularizers significantly outperform traditional gradient-based and reinforcement-learning methods across several tests, demonstrating substantial improvements in fidelity and robustness against noise model mismatches.
AI.conclusion: The regularizers lead to a marked reduction in control infidelity, achieving up to 50% improvement, indicating their potential for practical applications in open quantum systems.

title: Phase Transitions and Gravitational Wave Production at the End of Thermal Inflation
summary: We investigate the first-order phase transition that terminates thermal inflation and evaluate the associated stochastic gravitational-wave signals. The transition is first characterized through semi-analytic calculations of the bounce action, which are compared with numerical results obtained using CosmoTransitions. We then study its real-time evolution in a three-dimensional Langevin lattice simulation that incorporates Hubble expansion and the corresponding temperature evolution throughout the transition. The lattice dynamics are consistent with the bounce-action estimates: the transition proceeds through localized bubble nucleation and subsequent bubble growth, rather than through a phase-mixing instability. Using the resulting transition parameters, we estimate the gravitational-wave spectra generated by bubble collisions and acoustic motions in the plasma. The predicted stochastic background lies within the projected sensitivity ranges of future gravitational-wave observatories, including BBO and DECIGO.

AI.tldr: This study investigates the first-order phase transition that ends thermal inflation, analyzing gravitational-wave signals arising from this transition through semi-analytic and numerical methods.
AI.motivation: Understanding phase transitions in the early universe is crucial for cosmology and astrophysics, particularly regarding gravitational wave signals.
AI.method: The phase transition is studied using semi-analytic calculations and numerical simulations via CosmoTransitions and a Langevin lattice model that simulates Hubble expansion and temperature changes.
AI.result: The study finds that the transition involves localized bubble nucleation and growth, with dynamics consistent across methods. Estimates show that generated gravitational waves fall within future observatories' sensitivity ranges.
AI.conclusion: The findings indicate that there is a significant potential for detecting stochastic gravitational waves from this phase transition with upcoming observatories.

title: Majorana bound states in a hybrid Kitaev ladder with long-range pairing
comment: 11 pages, 11 figures, Submitted for review at Phys. Rev. B
summary: We investigate an inter-leg coupled hybrid Kitaev ladder composed of two parallel superconducting chains with distinct pairing interactions. The upper chain of the ladder hosts conventional $p$-wave pairing, while the lower chain exhibits long-range pairing that decays algebraically with distance. We demonstrate that the mutual influence of long-range pairing exponent, chemical potential, and inter-leg coupling strength gives rise to a rich topological phase diagram characterized by multiple Majorana zero modes and massive Dirac modes. In particular, we show that the inter-leg coupling renormalizes the effective energy scales, leading to a systematic shift of the topological phase boundaries and enabling controlled tuning of the Majorana modes. Furthermore, we identify a transition from a two Majorana zero mode phase to a phase encapsulating four Majorana zero modes, as the long-range pairing exponent is varied. This transition is accompanied by a crossover regime in which Majorana zero modes coexist with massive Dirac modes, reflecting hybridization between edge and bulk excitations. This ladder thus provides a minimal and attractive platform for realizing the impact of a long-range pairing on topological phases. Our results highlight the potential of long-range hybrid systems for engineering tunable topological states relevant for quantum information applications.

AI.tldr: The paper explores a hybrid Kitaev ladder with superconducting chains exhibiting different pairing types, demonstrating a complex topological phase diagram influenced by long-range pairing, chemical potential, and coupling strength.
AI.motivation: To understand how long-range pairing affects the topological properties in superconducting systems and to explore potential applications in quantum information.
AI.method: The study employs theoretical analysis to examine the interplay between long-range pairing, chemical potential, and inter-leg coupling in a hybrid Kitaev ladder, characterizing the resulting topological phases and modes.
AI.result: The findings reveal multiple Majorana zero modes and massive Dirac modes, with a transition from a two to four Majorana zero mode phase as the pairing exponent is varied, and indicative hybridization effects.
AI.conclusion: The research demonstrates the significant role of long-range pairing in shaping topological states, highlighting its potential for creating tunable quantum states in hybrid systems.

title: On chip, multifunctional quantum sensing using single spins in a van der Waals crystal
summary: Nanoscale thermometry and magnetometry are in high demand across a wide range of scientific and technological applications. In this context, optically addressable spins in solids have emerged at the forefront of on-chip quantum sensing. However, simultaneous quantum sensing of multiple parameters (e.g., temperature and magnetic field) using the same spin sensor remains challenging due to cross-sensitivity to multiple physical quantities. Here, we demonstrate independent dual sensing of temperature and magnetic field using single quantum emitters in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). We experimentally verify the independent response of the zero-phonon line (ZPL) position to temperature and of optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) to magnetic fields. Furthermore, we demonstrate local temperature sensing of a microcircuit while simultaneously measuring an external magnetic field. Our results establish quantum emitters in hBN as a robust platform for multifunctional quantum sensing under realistic operating conditions.

AI.tldr: Demonstration of independent dual sensing of temperature and magnetic fields using single quantum emitters in hexagonal boron nitride.
AI.motivation: To address the challenge of simultaneous sensing of multiple parameters using a single spin sensor due to cross-sensitivity.
AI.method: Utilization of optically addressable spins in hexagonal boron nitride for independent measurement of temperature and magnetic fields.
AI.result: Experimental verification of distinct responses of the zero-phonon line (ZPL) with temperature changes and of ODMR in magnetic fields; successful local temperature sensing while measuring external magnetic fields.
AI.conclusion: Quantum emitters in hBN are established as an effective platform for multifunctional quantum sensing in real-world scenarios.

title: The X17 Anomaly: Experimental Evidence and Theoretical Interpretations
summary: This review summarizes the experimental evidence for the hypothetical X17 particle, examines the theoretical frameworks in which it can be accommodated, and discusses its potential implications for the Standard Model and couplings to known particles. Future experimental prospects are also highlighted.

AI.tldr: The review discusses the X17 particle's experimental evidence, theoretical frameworks, implications on the Standard Model, and future experimental prospects.
AI.motivation: To explore the implications of the X17 particle on fundamental physics and its integration into existing theoretical models.
AI.method: The review synthesizes experimental data and theoretical perspectives on the X17 particle.
AI.result: Provides insights into how the X17 particle could influence the Standard Model and details opportunities for future research.
AI.conclusion: The X17 particle may have significant implications for particle physics, warranting further experimental investigation.

title: Optimal Shadow Estimation with Minimal Measurement Settings
comment: 8+21 pages and 3+5 figures; comments and suggestions are very welcome!
summary: Shadow estimation is a powerful framework for predicting quantum properties from randomized measurements. While $3$-design protocols achieve optimal worst-case performance, the minimal number of measurement bases required for such optimality has remained open. Here we prove that $Θ(d^2)$ measurement bases are both necessary and sufficient for worst-case optimal shadow estimation and construct an explicit basis family. In stark contrast, any state $2$-design already suffices for average-case optimality: the mean squared shadow norm of normalized observables is bounded by a universal constant, and we prove strong concentration for Haar-random states, yielding constant sample complexity for generic pure-state fidelity estimation. Easily implementable $2$-designs -- from mutually unbiased bases, cyclic measurements, or shallow $\mathcal{O}(\log n)$-depth circuits -- enable optimal average-case protocols with remarkably simple measurement strategies. Our results establish a fundamental complexity separation: worst-case estimation requires $Θ(d^2)$ bases, whereas average-case performance requires only $Θ(d)$ bases, with broad implications for quantum information theory and near-term experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the measurement bases needed for optimal shadow estimation in quantum properties, distinguishing between worst-case and average-case scenarios.
AI.motivation: To determine the minimal number of measurement bases required for optimal shadow estimation in quantum systems.
AI.method: The authors prove that $Θ(d^2)$ measurement bases are necessary and sufficient for worst-case optimality, and explore the implications of $2$-designs for average-case scenarios with a focus on sample complexity.
AI.result: $Θ(d^2)$ bases are needed for worst-case estimation, while $Θ(d)$ bases suffice for average-case; simple implementations achieve average-case optimality with minimal complexity.
AI.conclusion: The findings reveal a significant complexity difference between worst-case and average-case scenarios in quantum shadow estimation, influencing future quantum information theory and practical applications.

title: String Axiverse Enhancement of Superradiant Dark Matter Production
summary: We study the effects of string axion emission on dark matter production by light primordial black holes (PBHs), through both evaporation and superradiance. We show, in particular, that the Hawking emission of $\mathcal{O}(100-10^5)$ light axion species predicted in realistic string theory constructions can significantly enhance the efficiency of superradiance, given the associated increase in the PBH spin. The string axiverse thus significantly expands the parametric regions (dark matter mass and PBH mass and spin) for which a sizeable fraction of dark matter may presently be in the form of ``micro-boson stars'': the self-gravitating remnants of superradiant dark matter clouds. Conversely, for too large a number of axion species PBHs evaporate too quickly for superradiant clouds to attain their maximum mass. Finally, assuming that all dark matter is produced by PBHs (through both superradiance and Hawking emission), we show that the axions emitted during PBH evaporation give an immeasurably small contribution to the relativistic degrees of freedom at recombination.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how string axion emission influences dark matter production by primordial black holes (PBHs), particularly through evaporation and superradiance effects.
AI.motivation: The study aims to explore the impact of light axion emissions from string theory on the dynamics and characteristics of dark matter, specifically in the context of primordial black holes.
AI.method: The authors analyze Hawking emission of light axions and its effects on PBH spin and the formation of micro-boson stars, considering different parameter regions for dark matter and PBH properties.
AI.result: They find that realistic constructions of string theory can enhance superradiance efficiency, allowing a broader range of PBH characteristics to yield substantial dark matter in the form of micro-boson stars, but excessive axion species can hinder growth of superradiant clouds.
AI.conclusion: The study concludes that while PBHs can produce dark matter, axions emitted during their evaporation have a negligible impact on the relativistic degrees of freedom at recombination.

title: The use of Peres lattices in periodically driven systems
summary: We demonstrate the strength of the method of Peres lattices in periodically driven quantum systems. The method, which has previously been used mostly in stationary systems, enables us to efficiently detect resonances in the driven system, to monitor the onset of chaos, and to recognize critical properties of the Floquet modes. It also allows quick comparisons of the spectra of Floquet modes for various driving Hamiltonians and transparent tests of the iterative approximation techniques based on effective stationary Hamiltonians.

AI.tldr: This paper explores the application of Peres lattices in periodically driven quantum systems, highlighting their efficiency in detecting resonances, chaos onset, and critical Floquet mode properties.
AI.motivation: To prove the utility of Peres lattices for analyzing periodically driven quantum systems, an area where efficient resonance detection and chaos monitoring is critical.
AI.method: The authors apply the Peres lattice method to evaluate the spectral properties of Floquet modes in response to various driving Hamiltonians.
AI.result: The application reveals the ability to efficiently detect resonances, monitor chaos onset, and assess critical properties of Floquet modes.
AI.conclusion: Peres lattices significantly enhance the analysis of periodically driven quantum systems, providing a robust framework for spectral comparisons and iterative approximation techniques.

title: All-valid-state HOBO encoding for constrained combinatorial optimization on NISQ devices
comment: 14 pages, 11 figures. Corresponding author: Jun-ichi Shirakashi
summary: Continued advancements in quantum computing have stimulated growing interest in translating quantum technologies into real-world applications. Consequently, the investigation of practically motivated NP-hard problems is of significant value. This study investigates the performance of a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) in addressing the traveling salesperson problem (TSP) through noiseless simulations representative of noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices using higher-order binary optimization (HOBO) encodings. We construct a HOBO Hamiltonian with an efficient binary representation and propose an all-valid-state HOBO (AVS-HOBO) scheme based on cyclic mapping that eliminates one penalty term and reuses states that would otherwise be invalid. Using TSP instances of up to 20 cities, we compare the original HOBO and AVS-HOBO encodings from multiple perspectives, including the energy convergence behavior and the approximation, tour-length, and feasibility ratios. In addition to simulations, we perform computations on real quantum hardware with different device architectures, where we not only compare the performances of different chips but also investigate the effects of different error-mitigation methods on actual quantum machines. The results indicate that AVS-HOBO encoding enhances the practical reliability of VQE on NISQ devices and improves scalability for larger TSP instances, with broader applicability to constrained quantum optimization problems.

AI.tldr: This study evaluates a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) for the traveling salesperson problem (TSP) using higher-order binary optimization (HOBO) encodings and different error-mitigation strategies on quantum devices.
AI.motivation: Advancements in quantum computing necessitate practical applications for NP-hard problems, making this investigation valuable.
AI.method: The study employs noiseless simulations and analyzes a new all-valid-state HOBO (AVS-HOBO) scheme to optimize the VQE for TSP instances, comparing it with original HOBO encodings.
AI.result: AVS-HOBO encoding improves the reliability and scalability of VQE for larger TSP instances, outperforming traditional methods and benefiting from robust error mitigation.
AI.conclusion: The findings suggest that AVS-HOBO encoding not only enhances VQE performance for TSP on NISQ devices but also has implications for other constrained quantum optimization problems.

title: Rotating magnetized pion gas of finite transverse size: condensation constraints and transport properties
summary: This work investigates the electric, thermal, and thermoelectric responses of a rotating pion gas of finite transverse radius in the presence of a background magnetic field, with the rotation axis aligned with the magnetic field. We explicitly calculate the parameter limits for $π^+$ condensation and restrict our working regime safely outside these boundaries, ensuring well-behaved transport coefficients. Notably, the system exhibits a condensation asymmetry, with $π^-$ remaining uncondensed at the parameters that induce $π^+$ condensation. Using the Boltzmann Transport Equation under the Relaxation Time Approximation, we calculate the longitudinal electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, and the Seebeck coefficient. Our results reveal a competing interplay between the magnetic field and rotation, highlighting the substantial impact of rotation on the medium's transport properties: while the magnetic field suppresses the transport coefficients in a static medium, rotation, acting as an effective chemical potential, introduces an energy shift that favors their increase. Beyond an angular velocity, this rotational enhancement overpowers the magnetic suppression, leading to an increase in the transport coefficients with increasing magnetic field. Finally, we analyze the relative significance of charge and heat transport through the Lorenz number, providing further insight into the transport characteristics of the rotating magnetized pion medium.

AI.tldr: This study explores the effects of rotation and magnetic fields on the transport properties of a pion gas, revealing significant interactions between these elements and their influence on conductivity and thermoelectric responses.
AI.motivation: Understanding the transport properties of a rotating pion gas under a magnetic field is crucial for applications in high-energy physics and related fields.
AI.method: The Boltzmann Transport Equation under the Relaxation Time Approximation was employed to calculate the longitudinal electrical and thermal conductivities and the Seebeck coefficient, with a focus on parameter limits for $π^+$ condensation.
AI.result: Findings indicate a condensation asymmetry where $π^+$ condenses but $π^-$ does not under certain conditions. The interplay between rotation and the magnetic field significantly affects transport properties, with rotation enhancing transport coefficients despite magnetic suppression.
AI.conclusion: The research underscores the complex interplay of rotation and magnetic fields in altering the transport characteristics of the pion medium, especially beyond certain angular velocities where rotational effects become dominant.

title: Simulation of Non-Markovian Quantum Accelerated Dynamics via Time-Fractional Schrödinger Equation
summary: The Time-Fractional Schrödinger Equation (TFSE) is an effective tool for simulating the dynamics of non-Markovian quantum systems. The Quantum Speed Limit (QSL) time characterizes the minimum time required for the evolution of a non-Markovian quantum system. In this paper, Wei's TFSE is employed to simulate the non-Markovian quantum accelerated evolution process in the Resonant Dissipative Jaynes-Cummings (RDJC) model. By solving the QSL time of a time-fractional single-qubit open system, the enhancement mechanism of the system evolution speed induced by the non-Markovian memory effects of the environment is revealed. Further studies show that the optimized acceleration of the system evolution can be achieved by jointly regulating the fractional order, coupling strength, and photon number. Comparative analyses indicate that Wei's TFSE can accurately capture the non-Markovian accelerated dynamical features of the system over the entire fractional order range, whereas Naber's TFSE is applicable only within a limited fractional order interval. In addition, the comparisons of the average simulation time for calculating the dynamical trajectory of the excited-state probability demonstrate that Wei's TFSE has a significant simulation advantage in computational efficiency. Therefore, Wei's TFSE is more accurate and efficient for simulating the accelerated dynamics of non-Markovian quantum systems.

AI.tldr: Wei's Time-Fractional Schrödinger Equation effectively simulates the acceleration of non-Markovian quantum systems, demonstrating improved speed and computational efficiency.
AI.motivation: To explore efficient simulation methods for the dynamics of non-Markovian quantum systems using the QSL time as a measure of evolution speed.
AI.method: The study uses Wei's TFSE to analyze the RDJC model, focusing on the influence of non-Markovian memory effects on evolution speed and optimizing parameters such as fractional order and coupling strength.
AI.result: Wei's TFSE accurately represents the accelerated dynamics across a wider fractional order range compared to Naber's TFSE and shows a marked advantage in computational efficiency for simulating the excited-state probability trajectory.
AI.conclusion: Wei's TFSE is superior in accuracy and efficiency for simulating non-Markovian quantum system dynamics.

title: QPU-scale randomized benchmarking via Bell-pair injection
comment: Haripriya Pettugani, María Aguado-Yáñez and Astryd Park contributed equally to this work
summary: Mirror randomized benchmarking (MRB) is an established technique that provides a global error metric at the scale of a whole QPU. To expand upon this we introduce Mirror Quantum Awesomeness (MQA), a hybrid protocol that adds a structured entangling layer to MRB circuits. This enables per-edge correlation dynamics to be tracked via mutual information while preserving the MRB infidelity estimate. The resulting analysis of the injected entangled pairs locates a critical circuit depth, beyond which rudimentary error mitigation techniques can be expected to fail. A topological variant, Topological MQA, supplies a second critical depth via a decoder based on the surface-code decoding problem. Both are validated in simulation and demonstrated on the 156-qubit \texttt{ibm\_fez} and \texttt{ibm\_kingston} processors, where MQA closely agrees with MRB on the entanglement infidelity and the critical depth for \texttt{ibm\_fez} is found to be $\sim 50$.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Mirror Quantum Awesomeness (MQA), a hybrid protocol enhancing Mirror Randomized Benchmarking (MRB) by integrating a structured entangling layer to better assess quantum processing unit (QPU) error metrics and dynamics.
AI.motivation: To improve error analysis in quantum processors and identify limitations of basic error mitigation techniques.
AI.method: MQA utilizes a structured entangling layer in MRB circuits to track correlation dynamics through mutual information while retaining MRB's error estimates. A topological variant, Topological MQA, introduces a surface-code decoder to locate critical circuit depths.
AI.result: The study demonstrates that MQA closely aligns with MRB results on entanglement infidelity, identifying critical circuit depths—about 50 for the 	exttt{ibm ez} processor, where basic error mitigation falls short.
AI.conclusion: MQA enhances error analysis capabilities in QPUs by effectively tracking correlation dynamics, offering insights into circuit depth limits for error mitigation strategies.

title: Optimizing resource allocation for accuracy in noisy variational quantum algorithms
summary: For quantum algorithms to achieve their full potential, we need methodologies to optimize them, such as reaching a given output accuracy with minimal resource costs. Here, we develop such a methodology for a class of Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) algorithms. We leverage simulations of a Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) to propose a phenomenological model of such algorithms that captures the complex relationship between algorithmic accuracy, algorithmic resource costs, and the noise that exists in realistic quantum hardware. For this, we take the algorithmic resource cost to be the total number of quantum gate-operations in the algorithm; minimizing this cost typically makes the algorithm faster and more energy-efficient. We consider the subtle trade-off between quantum circuit size (small circuits are too imprecise, but large ones are too noisy), and the number of iterations of that quantum circuit for the full algorithm to sufficiently converge. Using a noise-metric-resource methodology, we identify the sweet spot (of circuit size versus iterations) that minimizes the algorithmic resource costs for a desired algorithm accuracy. It also gives the circuit size that maximizes algorithm accuracy for a fixed resource cost. Our methodology provides a practical guideline for near-term deployment of variational algorithms on realistic noisy hardware, including hardware that uses error mitigation.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a methodology to optimize Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) algorithms, focusing on minimizing resource costs while achieving desired accuracy.
AI.motivation: To enable quantum algorithms to perform efficiently, it is crucial to optimize them with minimal resource expenditures, especially in the NISQ era.
AI.method: The methodology utilizes simulations of the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) to develop a model that analyzes the trade-offs between accuracy, resource costs (quantum gate operations), and noise in quantum circuits.
AI.result: The study identifies optimal circuit sizes and iteration counts that balance algorithmic resource costs and accuracy, establishing guidelines for practical implementations on noisy quantum hardware.
AI.conclusion: The findings offer a framework for efficiently deploying variational quantum algorithms in realistic conditions, taking noise and error mitigation into account.

title: Multi-objective design of photon blockade for bright single-photon sources
summary: High-quality single-photon sources, realized through saturable emitters, photon blockade, or heralded pair generation, are indispensable building blocks for photonic quantum platforms. Although these mechanisms suppress multiphoton emission through distinct principles typically captured by analytical models, their practical implementation is constrained by conflicting requirements for purity, brightness, and indistinguishability, which must be balanced within high-dimensional design landscapes. Here, we propose a computational framework for optimizing competing metrics of single-photon sources. Building on a Liouville-space adjoint formulation that efficiently evaluates multiple objectives in Markovian open quantum systems, we develop a Jacobian-based update, which ensures first-order monotonic reduction of multi-objective costs. By incorporating simulated annealing to escape gradient-vanishing plateaus, our framework achieves a design success rate of nearly 60 % for photon blockade with g2(0) smaller than 0.1 and theoretically bounded brightness across a broad parameter space, without any analytical guidance. This framework provides a general recipe for multi-objective design of open quantum systems.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a computational framework for optimizing single-photon sources, enhancing performance metrics like purity, brightness, and indistinguishability through an effective optimization method.
AI.motivation: The need for high-quality single-photon sources in photonic quantum platforms necessitates balancing conflicting requirements such as purity, brightness, and indistinguishability.
AI.method: A computational framework using a Liouville-space adjoint formulation is developed, incorporating Jacobian-based updates and simulated annealing for multi-objective optimization in quantum systems.
AI.result: The framework achieves nearly 60% design success rate for photon blockade with g2(0) < 0.1 and ensures theoretically bounded brightness across varied parameters.
AI.conclusion: This framework provides a versatile approach for the multi-objective design of open quantum systems, enabling optimized single-photon source development.

title: Applications of quantum annealing to magnetic dipole hyperfine structure constants: First results beyond energies for atoms
summary: We report the first results of the magnetic dipole hyperfine structure (HFS) constants of neutral $\mathrm{Li}$, Li-like $\mathrm{Be}$, neutral $\mathrm{Na}$, and Na-like $\mathrm{Mg}$ using a modified version of the Quantum Annealer Eigensolver (QAE) algorithm on D-Wave's quantum hardware. The results are benchmarked against relativistic configuration interaction with multiconfiguration Dirac Hartree-Fock (MCDHF) calculations using the General-purpose Relativistic Atomic Structure Package (GRASP), and simulated annealing. In our modified QAE, a zooming-and-sigma-annealing approach with a floating-point encoding scheme is adopted to estimate the ground-state eigenvalue and eigenvector of the relativistic Dirac-Coulomb Hamiltonian matrices ($H_{\mathrm{DC}}$) constructed from 11 or fewer configuration state functions (CSFs). For calculations with extended correlation orbital sets, we applied a CSF truncation scheme, retaining only CSFs (up to 12) that make significant contributions to the ground-state wavefunction. Our modified QAE precision is kept limited to three decimal places (up to 10 qubits). Hardware demonstrations on the D-Wave quantum processing unit (QPU) yielded results that were completely consistent with GRASP (at the chosen precision) in determining the magnetic dipole HFS constants, with accuracy varying across systems and $H_{\mathrm{DC}}$ matrix dimensions.

AI.tldr: First results on magnetic dipole hyperfine structure constants of Li, Be, Na, and Mg using a modified Quantum Annealer Eigensolver on D-Wave's quantum hardware.
AI.motivation: To explore magnetic dipole hyperfine structure constants using quantum computational methods, which could enhance precision in atomic structure calculations.
AI.method: Utilized a modified Quantum Annealer Eigensolver with zooming-and-sigma-annealing and floating-point encoding to estimate eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the relativistic Dirac-Coulomb Hamiltonian.
AI.result: Results benchmarked against MCDHF calculations show consistency with GRASP in determining HFS constants, demonstrating accuracy across different systems and matrix dimensions.
AI.conclusion: The modified QAE provides a promising quantum computational approach for calculating atomic hyperfine structure constants, potentially improving upon traditional computational methods.

title: Quantum-Accelerated Self-Consistent Field: A Hybrid Algorithm
summary: We present the Grover adaptive search self-consistent field (GAS-SCF) algorithm. GAS-SCF leverages quantum arithmetic to construct an efficient oracle that marks target states (Fock states) which improve upon some initial classical energy estimate. Amplitude amplification then increases the probability of measuring these states. This approach offers a theoretical quadratic speed-up for the optimization problem encountered in SCF quantum chemistry and establishes a baseline against which structured optimization algorithms, such as QAOA and DQI may be compared. In this work, we classically simulate three examples as proofs of concept of the algorithm, the largest consisting of 26 qubits. We then extend our analysis to two larger systems, with O3 representing the largest case at 330 qubits. These examples are chosen to probe classically challenging SCF regimes. Achieving chemically relevant applications of GAS-SCF will require large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum hardware.

AI.tldr: The GAS-SCF algorithm uses quantum techniques to enhance SCF optimization in quantum chemistry, achieving theoretical improvements and showcasing its viability through classical simulations of up to 330 qubits.
AI.motivation: To improve the efficiency of self-consistent field (SCF) methods in quantum chemistry by leveraging quantum computing.
AI.method: The GAS-SCF algorithm uses a quantum oracle for marking target Fock states based on a classical energy estimate and applies amplitude amplification to boost measurement probabilities.
AI.result: The algorithm demonstrates a theoretical quadratic speed-up and successfully simulates systems up to 330 qubits, tackling classically difficult SCF problems.
AI.conclusion: GAS-SCF shows promise for future large-scale applications in quantum chemistry but necessitates advancements in quantum hardware.

title: Operator Learning for efficient Quantum Computation
summary: An efficient implementation of quantum algorithms is often hindered by the lack of efficient primitives for operators and state preparation. This limits both the ability of near-term quantum hardware to simulate complex problems and the potential of fault-tolerant algorithms to achieve practical quantum advantage. To address this, we propose a full-stack variational framework that transforms arbitrary operators to compact quantum circuits. The resulting variational circuits can be tailored to the connectivity and long-range interaction of the target hardware. The learning process employs backpropagation together with a cost function that efficiently optimizes unitary operators and non-unitary -- dense or sparse -- operators using only a single ancilla qubit for block encoding.
